A question about a preference read from someone's words, with the

oneOf.description:
"140,000: at least, or around? In which currency?" A pay without a
currency is never compared with any job's.

currency.description: As read; absent when the words didn't say (never assumed).

oneOf.description:
"Small teams: must have, or nice to have? The team you'd join, or
the company's size?" Asked when the words didn't make the stance
clear ("small teams" alone, "maybe small teams").

say ("remote, at least USD 140k"). Until answered it is read as a

ranges.description:

verified.description:

consider.description: What to consider: caveats, then unknowns (up to 3).

Useful practical facts (pay reaching the person's target, remote

summary.description: Role · level · stack · domain · pay · where.

unknowns.description:

why.description:

oneOf.description: The person has not dealt with it yet.

From every open job to what is on the feed. Every number is counted,

changed.description: Reviewed before and changed materially since.

new.description: Of those, new to the person.

passed_eligibility.description:
Left after eligibility, closed listings, pay minimums and what the

strong_fits.description: Of those, strong fits: what Today chooses from.

worth_reviewing.description: Of those, strong fits and jobs worth reviewing.

caught_up.description: Nothing new is worth the person's time right now.

items.description:
Best first. Few on purpose; empty when there is nothing new worth

passed_over.description:
Recommendations shown earlier that the person let pass (not shown
again unless they change).

verified_now.description: Listings verified while preparing the feed.

oneOf.description: Looked at it, no opinion. Carries no weight in learned taste.

reason.description: Why, in the person's own words. Stored verbatim (encrypted).

feedback_id.description: `fb_…` of the stored event (or the earlier one this repeats).

recorded.description:
Whether a new feedback event was stored. `false` means the request
repeated one already in effect (same action, same reason): nothing
changed, and retrying is safe.

taste_changed.description: Whether what JobHunt learned from feedback changed.

reason.description: The person's words, exactly as given.

checked.description: Open opportunities checked (matching the query, if any).

passed_eligibility.description:
Left after eligibility, closed listings, required pay minimums and
what the person already acted on (rejected, applied).

plausible.description: Of those, the ones ranked maybe or better.

worth_reviewing.description: Of those, the ones worth reviewing or a strong fit.

ambiguities.description: What was unclear, for the person to settle.

constraints_noted.description: Practical constraints the words mentioned (never taste).

outcome.description:
`read`, or `fallback` when a model couldn't be used and the rules

rejected.description: Statements the interpreter produced that failed validation.

decision.description: The decision brief (`None` without a profile).

description.description:

eligibility.description: Eligibility with its reasons (`None` without a profile).

job_id.description: `job_…` of the record the details are read from.

locations.description: Every location the source lists, primary first.

sources.description:
Every source record (provenance and per-source verification), when
requested.

JobNoteView.description: A reason about one job only (not generalized).

read_as.description: What it was read as ("avoid: this domain").

agrees.description: Whether the feedback agrees with what they said (explicit patterns).

basis.description: "2 reasons in your words and 1 action without a reason".

direction.description: `prefer` or `avoid`: the way the evidence leans.

reasons.description: Reasons in the person's words among the support.

stated.description: What the person said about it (explicit patterns).

status.description:
`active` (used in ranking), `mixed` (contradictory, not used),
`not_enough` (too little evidence yet) or `explicit` (the person
said something about it, which is used instead).

Learning.description: What feedback has taught so far.

active_patterns.description: Patterns learned from it that affect ranking now.

has_preferences.description:
The person has stated preferences (they always outrank learned
taste).

ListingState.description: The listing state one verification attempt found.

LocationControls.description:
Where the person lives and may work, and what to do when eligibility
is unclear. The job's own location, its remote scope, the person's work
authorization and relocation are separate things, kept apart.

authorized_in.description: Countries or regions the person stated they may already work in.

home.description:
Where the person lives, as written (from the preference, else the
resume header).

home_country.description: The country Narrow reads it as ("Brazil"); absent when unrecognized.

remote_geography.description: Geographies remote roles should be open to, with their stance.

Remote scopes that include where the person lives, broadest first
("anywhere", "the Americas", "Latin America", "South America",
"Brazil"). A posting that says only "Remote" is none of these.

unclear_eligibility.description:
`show` (marked unresolved; the default) or `hide` (until
eligibility is confirmed).

lower_tiers.description: Ranked maybe or low priority (`all_tiers` shows them).

Pay not published (or not comparable), and the person hides such
jobs.

unmet_requirement.description:
The posting contradicts something the person requires: a company
or team kind, their work setup, relocation, a remote geography.

NotificationSettingsView.description:

policy v2). At most one digest per local day, at `digest_time` on
`digest_days`, never inside quiet hours or while paused; nothing is
sent when nothing qualifies.

available.description: Whether this service can send email at all.

cadence.description:
Legacy (BRU-295): `immediate` or `daily`. Both now mean the daily
digest.

digest_size.description: Jobs in one digest at most (1 to `max_items`).

digest_time.description: Local time the digest is composed, `HH:MM`.

email_status.description:
`none`, `unconfirmed` (a link was sent; nothing else is sent until
it is followed) or `confirmed`.

next_digest_at.description:
When the next digest may go out (it goes out only if something
qualifies); absent while off.

quiet_start.description:
Nothing is sent from `quiet_start` to `quiet_end` (local, `HH:MM`;
equal: no quiet hours).

timezone.description:
The IANA timezone the schedule is read in; absent: not set yet
(UTC is used until it is).

currency.description:
ISO code; absent when the person's words didn't say (never
assumed: until it is set, pay isn't compared).

since.description: When the current stage was reached.

furthest.description: The furthest application stage reached (kept after withdrawing).

since.description: When the current stage was reached.

entries.description:
Offers first, then interviewing, applied, saved (and rejected, when
asked for); latest first within a stage.

read_as.description:
How Narrow reads it ("Brazil", "Latin America", "anywhere"); absent
when it doesn't recognize the place, which then never counts as
including anywhere.

oneOf.description: "I don't care about this."

Remote only, prefer remote, hybrid okay, on-site okay, or no

Whether the person needs visa sponsorship to work where they live.

sponsorship.

Employee or contractor; `require` for the only one accepted, `avoid`

oneOf.description:
What kind of job the person is looking for, in their words. Replaces

configured), keeping every decision the person made.

confirmed_at.description: When they last said it looks right.

constraints.description:
Whether they can take a job: work setup, where they live and may
work, relocation, pay floor.

learned.description: Patterns learned from feedback, kept apart from what they said.

looking_for.description: What the person is looking for, in their words.

looking_for_source.description:
`description` (what they described), `statements` (their earlier
words, not yet interpreted as a description), or absent.

needs_confirmation.description: The summary has statements Narrow read that they haven't reviewed.

roles.description: "What kind of role are you looking for?".

set_aside.description:
Readings that go against a kind of role they chose ("avoid AI" when
they chose ML product work): not in effect, for them to settle.

supporting.description:
Kinds of work read or inferred that their choice of roles comes
before: context, not wanted.

understood.description: What Narrow understands they want, one line per dimension.

unsure.description: Weak inferences, not part of the summary unless confirmed.

TasteSourceView.description: Where one statement comes from, readable.

interpreted.description:
The words were interpreted by this call (false when the same input
was already interpreted).

preferences.description:
For a description: the practical constraints and structured
preferences read from the words.

contradictory.description: Patterns the evidence contradicts: not used.

controls.description:
The same preferences as structured controls (work setup,
relocation, location, pay, company and team), each in its layer.

covered_by_stated.description:
Patterns about something the person also stated: what they said is
used.

emerging.description: Patterns with too little evidence to use yet.

job_notes.description: Reasons about single jobs, not generalized.

learned.description: Patterns learned from feedback that affect ranking now.

stated.description:
What the person said: preferences in effect (they always win over
anything learned).

statements.description: The person's statements, verbatim, with what was not understood.

unread_reasons.description: Reasons nothing could be read from, kept as written.

TechnologyEvidence.description: A technology or skill and what backs it.

last_used.description: `current`, or the last year it was used ("2023").

strength.description:
`demonstrated` (used in an experience or project), `user_stated`,
`listed` (only in a skills list) or `unsupported`.

used_at.description: Where it was used ("Senior Engineer at Acme").

TechnologyMatch.description: A technology the job names, and the person's usable evidence for it.

evidence.description: Usable evidence (empty when there is none).

TokenView.description: A personal access token (never its secret).

UnreadReasonView.description: A reason nothing could be read from, kept as written.

UnresolvedClaim.description:
A claim waiting for the person's decision. Not usable as a fact until
confirmed.

about.description:
What it is about ("Senior Engineer at Acme", a project's name);
absent for the profile in general.

basis.description: For inferred claims: what the inference rests on.

confidence.description: How sure the reading is: `high`, `medium` or `low`.

document.description: The file (or account) the words are from.

evidence.description:
Every source that says it, its main one first (a resume and a
LinkedIn export both listing a position): the detail behind
`snippet`.

provenance.description:
`extracted` (read from a source), `inferred` (concluded by JobHunt)
or `user_entered`.

section.description: The section the words are from.

snippet.description: The source's own words behind it, verbatim (its main source).

UpdateNotificationsRequest.description: `PUT /api/v1/notifications`. Absent fields are left as they are.

cadence.description: Legacy: `immediate` or `daily` (both mean the daily digest).

email.description:
The address to notify. A new address is sent a confirmation link;
nothing else is sent to it until it is confirmed.

paused_until.description: Pause until then (at most a year ahead); `null` resumes.

quiet_start.description: `HH:MM`; equal start and end: no quiet hours.

UpdatePreferencesParams.description:
Arguments of `update_preferences`. Give at least one of `statement`,
`set` or `remove`.

remove.description: Preference (pref_…) or statement (stmt_…) ids to remove.

statement.description:
What the person wants, in their own words, e.g. "I want small
product teams, backend or platform work, remote from Brazil, at
least USD 120k". Stored verbatim; what JobHunt understands from it
is returned, including the parts it didn't understand.

UsableBasis.description: Why a fact may be used.

oneOf.description: The person confirmed it.
The person entered it.
Quoted directly from the current resume, with high confidence.

authority.description:
Who publishes the listing the state rests on
(`employer_configured_ats`, `employer_first_party`, …).

not_trusted_because.description: Why it is not trusted, when it isn't.

source.description: The source the state rests on (`greenhouse:stripe`).

trusted.description: Recent enough, from an authoritative source, to recommend on.

verified_at.description: When the last successful verification happened (RFC 3339).

last_attempt_at.description: The latest attempt at the record the state rests on.

last_success_at.description: The latest attempt that reached an answer.

listing.description: The listing state of the record the opportunity rests on.

recommendable.description: Trusted and the person appears able to take it.

reused.description:
Records whose recent attempt (within the reuse window) was reused
instead of asking the source again.

sources.description: Every source record with its latest attempt.

uncertainty.description:
What is uncertain: unknowns from the attempts, failures, and
disagreements between sources.

VerificationState.description:
What JobHunt believes about the listing, from verification and
discovery.

Withheld.description: Claims left out, by why. Their text is never included.

how_to_review.description: How the person can review them.

needs_review.description:
Inferred, uncertain, or no longer in the resume: usable once the
person confirms them.

rejected.description: Rejected by the person: never used.

WorkControls.description: Remote, hybrid or on-site, and relocation: two separate answers.

custom.description: The stored work modes in words, when `setup` is `custom`.

setup.description:
`remote_only`, `prefer_remote`, `hybrid_okay`, `onsite_okay`,
`no_preference`, or `custom` when the stored work modes are none of
those (a statement said "hybrid, not on-site"; see `custom`).

setup_records.description: The work-mode preferences behind the answer.

WorkSetupInput.description:
How the person wants to work, as one answer. Each is stored as the
work-mode preferences it means, replacing any others:

| Answer | Stored | Layer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `remote_only` | remote: required | requirement: hybrid or on-site jobs are a stated conflict |
| `prefer_remote` | remote: wanted | preference: ranking only |
| `hybrid_okay` | remote or hybrid: required | requirement: on-site jobs are a stated conflict |
| `onsite_okay` | on-site: acceptable | preference: nothing is ruled out |
| `no_preference` | nothing | — |

Work setup is not relocation (a separate answer), nor where the person
may legally work.
